title: War
hookLine: Christians pray for peace and for those who fight, and grieve all the dead

lines: A CHURCH IN A COUNTRY AT WAR.
PRAYERS FOR EVERYONE, EVEN THE ENEMY.
cards: On a Sunday morning, in a church in a country at war, the prayers reach the part where the names are read. A soldier's mother sits in the third row. Two rows back sits a family who fled the fighting with one suitcase.
In some churches, the prayers that morning ask for peace, for those who serve, for the wounded, for the leaders, and, following Jesus's words about loving enemies, for the enemy. All in one breath.
It's a hard place to stand, and a hard question for the faith.

teach.b: Begin with the hope. Isaiah sees a day when the nations "shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks: nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more."

Weapons melted into farm tools. A psalm says of God, "He maketh wars to cease unto the end of the earth; he breaketh the bow, and cutteth the spear in sunder." Here, war is not how things are meant to be.
Then Jesus, on a hillside: "Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God." Not the peace lovers. The peacemakers.
Peace is something you make, often at a cost. Christians have answered a world at war in different ways.
Some churches, like the Mennonites and the Quakers, hold that followers of Jesus should not take up arms at all, pointing to his words about loving enemies and turning the other cheek.

teach.h: NO ARMS, OR A JUST WAR?
teach.b: Others, including the Catholic Church and a number of Protestant churches, follow the just war tradition, linked with Augustine and Thomas Aquinas: war may sometimes be permitted, only for a just cause such as protecting the innocent, only as a last resort, and always under strict limits.
And there's a small scene in Luke. Soldiers ask John the Baptist what they should do. He doesn't tell them to leave the army.
He says, "Do violence to no man, neither accuse any falsely; and be content with your wages."

teach.h: ALL THE DEAD ARE SOMEONE'S CHILDREN.
teach.b: Across all these answers, the dead on both sides are still someone's children. Christians who disagree about war can still pray at the same graveside.

how: Christians pray for peace in public worship, for those in the armed forces and for victims of war; some churches, such as the Mennonites and Quakers, hold to nonviolence, while Catholic teaching and other churches follow the just war tradition, and Christians on both sides run relief work for refugees and the wounded.

o: a question every church answers the same way, from the same verses
something the Bible praises as the surest path to a lasting peace
something Isaiah hopes will end, which Christians answer in different ways

s: all Christians agree on whether war can be just
some churches hold to nonviolence, and others follow the just war tradition.
John the Baptist tells the soldiers to leave the army
he tells them to do violence to no man, accuse no one falsely, and be content with their wages.
Jesus blesses the peacemakers, not only the peace lovers
"blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God."

games.q: you're a soldier standing in the crowd at the river Jordan. you ask John the Baptist what you should do. what does he say?
o: do violence to no man, accuse no one falsely, be content with your wages.
games.why: Luke records exactly that. John doesn't tell them to quit, and doesn't bless the fighting either. he asks for no cruelty, no lies, and no grabbing.

practice: Bring to mind one war happening now, and picture one ordinary person on each side: someone in uniform, someone sheltering in a basement. Then picture the ones who would be called the enemy, and hold them too.
If you pray, you can pray Isaiah's line for all of them, that nation shall not lift up sword against nation; if you don't, simply hold them in your heart.

wordCard.voice: War. In Isaiah's hope, something to be beaten into plowshares; for Christians, something they answer in different ways, while grieving every life it takes.

carryVoice: Your line: blessed are the peacemakers. Jesus says they shall be called the children of God. Until tomorrow.
